events.title: "I've Been Meaning to Read That..." Adult Book Club: Lessons in Chemistry
events.description: Join us for a relaxed book discussion series dedicated to the books you’ve always meant to read but haven’t gotten to yet! Lessons in Chemistry by Bonnie Garmus Elizabeth Zott is not your average woman. In fact, Elizabeth Zott would be the first to point out that there is no such thing as an average woman. But it's the 1960s, and despite the fact that she is a scientist, her peers are very unscientific when it comes to equality. The only good thing to happen to her on the road to professional fulfillment is a run-in with her superstar colleague Calvin Evans (well, she stole his beakers). The only man who ever treated her ideas as equal, Calvin, is already a legend and a Nobel nominee. He's also awkward, kind, and tenacious. Theirs is true chemistry. But as events are never as predictable as chemical reactions, three years later, Elizabeth Zott is an unwed, single mother (did we mention it's the early 60s??) and the star of America's most beloved cooking show, "Supper at Six". Elizabeth's singular approach to cooking ('take one pint of H2O and add a pinch of sodium chloride') and independent example are proving revolutionary. Because Elizabeth isn't just teaching women how to cook, she's teaching them how to change the status quo. Whether you’re discovering this title for the first time or revisiting it, join the conversation and connect with fellow book lovers. We can’t wait to see you there!

events.title: Views of Nature The Galapagos Archipelago
events.description: These islands and the surrounding ocean are a stunning wildlife sanctuary. 97% of this vast area is a national park administered by the government of Ecuador as a permanent sanctuary for the many species of flora and fauna found here. Many of these are unique to the Galapagos while others visit this area on their migrations. Although the animals are varied, they share one trait; they are very tolerant of human presence. This affords visitors the opportunity to be close and observe natural behavior. Although most people do think of the wildlife when they hear Galapagos, the human history and culture up to the present day are an important part of the area that we present as well. This program tours the islands, with superb images of the animals and plant life, we also give our audience a view of the present human population centers as well as an introduction to the geology and the human history of the archipelago. events.description: “One little reader left in the library all alone; he closed the final book—and then there were none.” Join us for a year-long tribute to The Queen of Crime herself, Agatha Christie. The master of mystery and misdirection. Each month, enjoy book discussions, films, crafts, and special events inspired by her most captivating stories. Discover the intrigue, suspense, and brilliance that have thrilled readers for generations! Uncover the science behind the mystery! Agatha Christie: Forensics Through the Ages invites learners and mystery lovers alike to explore how real forensic breakthroughs shaped the world of detective fiction. From the early days of fingerprinting and toxicology to the rise of modern profiling, this program traces the fascinating intersection of crime-solving and storytelling through the lens of the world’s best-selling mystery writer. Discover how Christie’s background in pharmacy and her keen scientific curiosity brought authenticity to her plots—and how her stories continue to inspire forensic science today. Collect a passport sticker toward a mystery prize!

events.title: Makerspace Open Studio
events.description: I​nterested in 3D printing, laser cutting & engraving, Cricut, or looking for a space to work on your personal maker projects? Our drop-in makerspace offers a range of maker equipment for craftspeople of any skill level! Our equipment is free to use and are first come, first serve. Some materials are provided, on a limited basis. Outside materials are permitted, subject to staff approval. Maximum 2 projects per day per patron, dependent on makerspace usage. No projects may begin within the last 15 minutes of open studio.​ Patrons must be at least 12 years old or accompanied by an adult to use the Makerspace and are required to sign a behavior agreement during their first visit of the calendar year. Hours: Monday 3pm-7pm Tuesday 3pm-7pm Wednesday 3pm-7pm Thursday 10am-2pm Friday 10am-2pm 2nd Saturday of the month 10:00am-2:00pm 3D Printing Makers are welcome to one 3D print project at a time. Maximum print time: 2 hours. New print requests can only be made after previous prints are completed. Color and material are limited to what is already loaded at the time of printing. Outside materials are not permitted for 3D printing. Laser Cutting/Engraving (Glowforge) Makers are welcome to one 6” x 6” sheet of wood or 4” x 4” sheet of acrylic per week* while supplies last. Outside materials are permitted, subject to staff approval. Projects are limited to 30 minutes. Die cutting (Cricut Machine) Makers are welcome to one 12” x 12” sheet of permanent vinyl, removable vinyl, or iron on vinyl per week* while supplies last. Color availability varies. Outside materials are permitted, subject to staff approval. Projects are limited to 30 minutes. Low-Tech Crafting Alongside our machines and technology, we offer plenty of hands-on, “low-tech” crafting options like button making, Perler beads, painting, and more. Projects may change based on availability and interest, so there’s always something new to try. Stop by our Makerspace to see what you can create!
